config.title: Build typed cache interface

intro.title: Build typed cache interface
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a typed cache interface in TypeScript to store and retrieve data with type safety. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's generic types to create a flexible interface that works with different data types. The main constructs involved are interfaces, generics, and methods for setting and getting values. By the end, you'll have a reusable cache interface that ensures your data is consistently typed.
intro.usecase: Typed cache interfaces are essential in modern web applications where data consistency and type safety are critical. In e-commerce dashboards, they ensure product inventory data remains synchronized across multiple views without type errors. Search filters and user preference panels use typed caches to maintain state between page navigation while providing autocomplete suggestions with proper type validation. This pattern prevents runtime errors in financial applications where cached currency rates or stock prices must be type-safe across real-time updates.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface that defines the structure of a generic cache.
Implement a class that satisfies the cache interface using a Map for storage.
Apply generic type parameters to create a cache that works with any data type.
Manipulate the cache by writing methods to set, get, and delete items.
Configure the cache to handle optional retrieval with a default value.
Initialize a typed cache instance and populate it with sample data.
Control cache behavior by integrating a size limit or expiration logic.

steps.title: Initialize cache storage with Map data structure
steps.instruction: Inside your SimpleCache class, add a private field named 'storage' of type Map<K, V> to store cache items.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript's Map with generic types K and V to ensure type safety for keys and values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The SimpleCache class will have a private Map field ready to store typed key-value pairs.
successCriteria: SimpleCache class contains a private 'storage' field of type Map<K, V> initialized with new Map().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a type-safe Map to store cache items.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the field is private, named 'storage', and typed as Map<K, V>.
steps.feedbackWrong: The SimpleCache class should have a private Map field. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Implement set method with type safety
steps.instruction: Inside your SimpleCache class, implement the set method to store a key-value pair in the cache Map. The method should accept a key of type K and a value of type V, and return void.
steps.hint: Use the Map's set method to store the pair. Remember to match the signature defined in your Cache interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your SimpleCache class will have a working set method that stores typed key-value pairs in the internal Map.
successCriteria: The set method is implemented with the correct signature (key: K, value: V): void and uses this.storage.set(key, value).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Check that your method signature matches the Cache interface and uses the Map's set method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The set method is missing or incorrect. Ensure it accepts a key of type K and value of type V, and stores them using this.storage.set.

steps.title: Add clear method to Cache interface
steps.instruction: Add a clear method signature to your existing Cache interface. The method should have no parameters and return void.
steps.hint: Look for the Cache interface definition in your code and add a new method signature inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Cache interface will include a clear method signature, extending its contract.
successCriteria: The Cache interface has a clear method with no parameters and void return type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a method, but check the signature: it should have no parameters and return void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clear method signature is missing or incorrect. It should be added to the Cache interface with no parameters and void return type.

steps.title: Implement clear method in SimpleCache
steps.instruction: Add the clear method implementation to your SimpleCache class to remove all stored items.
steps.hint: The clear method should call the clear method on the Map instance (this.storage).
steps.expectedOutcome: The SimpleCache class will have a clear method that empties the storage Map.
successCriteria: The SimpleCache class includes a clear method that calls this.storage.clear()
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a clear method, but check that it correctly calls this.storage.clear() to remove all items.
steps.feedbackWrong: The clear method implementation is missing or incorrect. Add a clear method to SimpleCache that calls this.storage.clear().
